prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1093; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane at a traffic signal when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. The impact was consistent with a moderate rear-end collision, and both vehicles sustained visible damage at the rear and front respectively. Driver 1 reported neck strain at the scene and was evaluated by responding medical personnel. Driver 2 stated that the light had changed and that braking was delayed. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and the location of the main impact damage. No independent witnesses were located, and no other vehicles were involved. Several light scratches on the rear bumper of Driver 1's vehicle appear older than the present damage, and it could not be determined from the scene whether all of the damage resulted from this impact. The passenger in Driver 1's vehicle was not injured. Driver 1 was identified as the named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle. The name of the claimant was not provided at the scene, and a claim was reported by the same individual several days later.
